entities.name: CBG
observations: Cannabigerol is a non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid tested orally in male Lister hooded rats at 30–240 mg/kg.

entities.name: PMID:27503475
observations: Primary study: male Lister hooded rats received oral CBG or placebo; pre-satiated rats were monitored for 2 hours.
CBG at 120–240 mg/kg more than doubled total food intake and increased meal number; 240 mg/kg reduced latency to feed, without increasing individual meal size or duration.
No adverse effects were detected in open-field, static-beam, or grip-strength tests at 30–120 mg/kg.
Authors describe this as the first demonstration that CBG elicits hyperphagia and report no negative neuromotor side effects.

entities.name: CBG hyperphagia
observations: In pre-satiated male Lister hooded rats, oral CBG at 120–240 mg/kg more than doubled 2-hour food intake versus placebo and increased meal frequency.
At 240 mg/kg, CBG reduced latency to feed but did not significantly increase individual meal size or duration.

entities.name: CBG tolerability
observations: Short-term testing found no adverse effects on open-field, static-beam, or grip-strength parameters after oral CBG at 30–120 mg/kg in male Lister hooded rats.
This supports absence of detected neuromotor side effects, but does not establish comprehensive or long-term safety.

entities.name: PMID:28125508
observations: A later study found a THC-free, CBG-rich Cannabis sativa extract increased food intake after a 2-hour prefeed satiation procedure in male Lister-hooded rats.
The extract increased intake at 120 and 240 mg/kg and did not significantly alter ambulatory activity or rearing.
